w10_T4_000849: A workshop had 222 wooden boards to start. They multiplied supply by 9 through restocking. They added 65 more boards from a delivery. They added 10 boards from recycled materials. They multiplied the total by 9 for project planning. They multiplied by 8 for production expansion. The warehouse cost 1500 dollars per month. How many boards did the workshop have?
w10_T4_000851: A toy maker started with 12 action figures. He multiplied inventory by 6 through new production. He added 49 figures to the display case. He multiplied by 9 for the toy fair. He multiplied by 7 for regional distribution. He had gifted 20 figures to charity last year. How many figures did he have in stock?
w10_T4_000852: A bakery had 121 cookies this morning. By afternoon, 112 were sold to customers. They multiplied remaining cookies by 8 for the next batch. How many cookies did the bakery have at closing?
w10_T4_000854: A warehouse started with 231 items on Monday. Tuesday they removed 112 for shipping. They added 52 new items Wednesday. They added 53 items Thursday. They multiplied the stock by 8 for inventory count. They removed 1267 damaged items for disposal. The facility employed 15 workers. How many items remained in the warehouse?
w10_T4_000855: A coach had 77 baseballs to work with. He added 20 more for practice. He multiplied the supply by 7 times. He removed 648 old balls from storage. He multiplied the remaining by 4 for league play. The team had 25 players total. How many baseballs did the coach have ready?
w10_T4_000858: A farm started morning with 232 eggs from chickens. They multiplied the collection by 7 through afternoon laying. They added 39 eggs from a neighboring farm. w10_T4_000860: A gardener had 20 seed packets initially on Monday. He added 52 packets Tuesday morning. He added 37 packets Wednesday afternoon. He added 15 packets Thursday evening. How many seed packets did he have?
w10_T4_000862: A bookstore had 172 paperbacks on the shelf initially. They added 75 more from a shipment. They added 76 additional copies for a sale. They removed 179 damaged books. w10_T4_000867: A student started with 41 coins in a jar on Monday. He removed 11 coins for purchases on Tuesday. He doubled his collection by finding more coins. He added 43 coins from his allowance. w10_T4_000868: A warehouse received 223 boxes Monday morning. They added 79 more boxes Tuesday afternoon. They added 75 boxes Wednesday evening. w10_T4_000869: A baker had 150 loaves of bread initially. He divided them equally by 3 for different shops. He then multiplied that share by 3. He multiplied by 6 for a catering event. w10_T4_000876: A factory started with 57 units on Monday. They multiplied by 4 through morning production. They multiplied by 8 for afternoon shifts. They multiplied by 2 for quality control batches. w10_T4_000877: A collector had 119 stamps initially. He multiplied his collection by 9 through purchases. He multiplied by 9 again for the rare set. He multiplied by 6 for international stamps. He added 5 more valuable stamps. His friend had 50 stamps. How many stamps did the collector have?
w10_T4_000881: A store had 134 toys to sell on Monday. They multiplied inventory by 7 through restocking. They added 10 more toys from a donation. They removed 122 toys for a warehouse sale. w10_T4_000882: A farm had 181 eggs collected by morning. They added 69 more from afternoon collection. They divided the total equally by 5 for packaging. They added 41 eggs from evening laying. w10_T4_000884: A builder had 67 boxes of supplies initially. He multiplied by 4 for project expansion. He multiplied by 2 for team members. He added 38 boxes from a shipment. He removed 45 boxes for other sites. His foreman worked 10 years. How many boxes remained on site?
w10_T4_000887: A store started with 82 items on the shelf Monday. They multiplied by 8 through afternoon stocking. They multiplied by 2 for evening expansion. w10_T4_000889: A factory produced 210 units initially. They multiplied by 8 for a large order. They added 79 bonus units. They multiplied by 5 for packaging lots. w10_T4_000890: A warehouse had 150 boxes Monday morning. They multiplied by 3 through the day. They multiplied by 2 for shipment organization. They added 58 boxes from a delivery. They removed 184 boxes for store distribution. The building was 5000 square feet. How many boxes remained?
w10_T4_000894: A farm started with 84 apples initially. They multiplied by 5 through harvest. They added 23 apples from a neighbor. They multiplied by 6 for packing. w10_T4_000897: A warehouse had 159 boxes of supplies initially. They removed 62 boxes for immediate use. They multiplied remaining by 5. They removed 354 boxes for distribution. w10_T4_000901: A student had 177 coins initially. They multiplied by 3 through pocket money. They removed 529 coins for a purchase. They added 74 coins from a gift. They added 6 more coins found. His brother had 30 coins too. How many coins did the student have?
w10_T4_000902: A shop had 93 items on display starting out. They removed 6 for breakage. They added 64 from a new shipment. They removed 85 for store rearrangement. They removed 48 for returns processing. They removed 11 more damaged items. Converting to shifts of work took hours. How many items remained in the shop?
w10_T4_000915: A collector had 174 cards initially. They removed 44 for trading. They added 32 from a purchase. They divided by 2 for album organization. They multiplied by 7 for complete sets. Each card cost 5 cents. How many cards did they have in complete sets?
w10_T4_000917: A fund started with 127 dollars donated. They added 19 dollars Monday. They added 61 dollars Tuesday. They multiplied by 4 through grant matching. They added 45 dollars from a raffle.
